dimensions.note: apiToken stays .meta({sensitive:true}) and vault-supplied. create_label adds no credential field; vreq errors carry method/path/status/body only, never the token. Test fixtures use http://vikunja.test and tk_test.

Every new log line is a constant template with structured props (create_label: 'Created label {labelId} {title}' / 'already exists'; restoreBucket warning; warnTruncated warning). The logging test now includes create_label and asserts no digits or task ids are interpolated into message text.

create_label refuses without humanInstructed before any request (test asserts zero reads), validates hexColor in the schema, and throws naming the label id when a created label reads back wrong. reorder now catches every apply failure, writes the reorderPlan with converged=false and the error, then rethrows, so a failed run is never silent and never loses its evidence. set_due_date restores a dropped bucket and throws only if the move back did not land.

82 tests (67 before). New: create_label refusal/creation/idempotency (case-insensitive, beyond page 1)/colour read-back/bad colour; apply_plan and new_task still refuse unknown labels; reorder 99-card Backlog + 4-card Waiting converges (fails on 2026.10.15.1), non-convergence names Waiting with per-bucket counts and the repeated card and writes the plan first, 4028 give-up writes the plan; set_due_date bucket restore and apply_plan due op on an un-bucketing server (both fail on 2026.10.15.1); board/audit truncated false/true; writes refuse a truncated board or label read; vikunjaTask keeps unlisted fields while boardSnapshot keys are exact. The fake writeResource still fails any run that writes one instance name twice.

create_label reads every label page and returns an existing case-insensitive match with status exists, never a duplicate; a truncated label list refuses rather than risking a duplicate. reorder re-reads after every move as before. set_due_date is still a no-op write when the date already matches.

create_label uses PUT /labels (create) and GET /labels/{id} (read-back), Vikunja v2 label endpoints; hex_color is sent without '#', as Vikunja stores it. Paged reads keep honouring max_items_per_page and now report truncation at the 100-page cap instead of returning silently.
No new handles; every fetch keeps its AbortController timeout. Truncation caps the number of requests at 100 pages per read, as before.

README/manifest examples use generic names (homelab-backlog, example label titles). No internal hosts, IPs, vaults or buckets in code, tests, commit messages or the PR body; the pre-push denylist hook is run on push.

Resolved (#265): the model's own resource schemas (summary, boardAudit, reorderPlan, dueReport, boardSnapshot, planResult, new label) are plain z.object and strip unknown keys; a probe with .strict() on all of them passed the full suite, so no producer relied on extra keys. vikunjaTask and its label refs keep .passthrough() deliberately, with a comment: the record is the task as Vikunja returned it and readers use unlisted fields (index, identifier, ...). New argument schemas are typed with refinements.
New label spec declares lifetime infinite and garbageCollection 10; the others are unchanged.
Labels gain create (create_label) alongside read; rename/delete are out of scope by design (card #503). Cards: create/read/update/close as before; delete intentionally absent.

Won't do as swamp checks, with reason (closes the follow-up carried since 2026.09.26.1): the guards need the task as read inside the method (done flag, updated, bucket), apply_plan must apply the same rules per op mid-run where a check cannot run, swamp checks get raw unparsed args and cannot write a record, and a check would add --skip-checks as a second, unlogged bypass beside force/humanInstructed. Instead the rules are named functions shared by every surface: guardProblem/guardWrite, readinessProblems, requireBucketOf, and new clearWaitingDueProblem (set_due_date and apply_plan's due op).

create_label writes one label-<id> per run. reorder writes reorder-<project> exactly once on success or failure (the catch path writes and rethrows; the success path is not reached). set_due_date still writes task-<id> once, now from a re-read after any bucket restore so the recent-edit guard sees the latest updated.
The guard reads prior state via context.readResource('task-<id>'); no direct dataRepository access.

model.version and manifest 2026.10.22.1 with an upgrades entry; global arguments are unchanged, so attributes carry over. New resource fields (truncated, movesByBucket, repeatedMoves, error) have defaults, so earlier stored records still parse.
